claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside a package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends strategies for structuring the Git repositories used to publish packages; following these practices improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages.
The internal link /docs/iac/concepts/packages/ (Pulumi packages concept page) exists, as does /docs/iac/concepts/components/.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), each versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
A source-based package's version is the Git tag on its repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
The link target /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/packaging-components/#source-based-plugin-packages and /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/ exist.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry requires applying a semver Git tag (e.g., v1.2.3) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` step often runs automated tests before publishing.
The link target /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/ exists.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
The link target /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/packaging-components/#executable-based-plugin-packages exists.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; Pulumi recommends this.

A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep (forcing unrelated work to share a version) or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
A 1:1 repository-to-package mapping keeps git tags, release artifacts, and version history aligned.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and expected; the components ship together at the package's version.

Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components inside that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) to manage distinct packages.
The importance of the one-package-per-repository principles grows as an organization's Pulumi adoption grows.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (at https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Pulumi EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
The Pulumi EKS package in the Registry is a single package (with multiple components) — used as a reference example of cohesion.
A Pulumi package repository defines the package with a single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root, with components living alongside it.
The example repository layout places PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repo root and components under a components/ directory (components/EksCluster/, components/EksIam/) as a valid single-package layout.

Using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components is technically possible, but Pulumi does not recommend it because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
Semantic versioning is how consumers know whether a given change is a bug fix, a new feature, or a breaking change.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.

In the example sequence, an enhancement to ComponentA releases the package at v1.1.0 (from v1.0.0), and a subsequent breaking change to ComponentB releases the package at v2.0.0, illustrating semver bumps (minor for feature, major for breaking change).
Splitting unrelated components across separate, right-sized packages preserves the semver contract and keeps the upgrade story honest for platform teams that consume the packages.
The link target /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/ exists.
